headline: Ward 45's three calmest-looking rankings all reach the ward the same indirect way.
summary:
Three of Ward 45's six best rankings look like three separate confirmations of a calm, safe place, but none of them is a direct count of anything that happened here. Loneliness and violent crime both land the ward in the top two or three citywide, and both are estimated by spreading survey and crime data across census tracts by land area rather than by where people actually live. The modeled odds of residents fearing to walk alone at night place the ward third by a different route, a demographic model built from national survey data rather than a local count, and the source grades that one low confidence too. Those are three measures of three different things, sharing one weakness in how each one reaches the ward line. The crime figure is still built on offenses that were reported somewhere, and it genuinely runs low here. The fair read is that Ward 45 is quiet and that these three numbers are not three independent proofs of it.

A different set of numbers traces back to one office's decisions about how to spend the ward's aldermanic menu money, and nearly all of it went to one place. Street resurfacing took 99.4 percent of last year's pot, the second-highest share of any ward in the city. Because that pot only holds so much, the same decision explains why sidewalks got zero percent, dead last in Chicago, and why bike and pedestrian redesign work also got zero, 49th of fifty. The measure that scores how spread the spending is across project types lands near the bottom too, at 1.2 out of 100, the same concentration counted a different way. None of it passed through a resident vote either, since Ward 45 runs no participatory budgeting process of its own.
reading_the_rankings: Take the rodent baiting number before assuming Ward 45 has slow city service. Requests here close in 4.2 days on average, which sounds quick on its own, and it still ranks 49th of fifty, because most of the rest of Chicago closes the same request even faster. The rank describes how fast other wards are, not how slow this one is. The TIF number needs a similar correction. Ward 45's $579,553 in captured tax increment dollars ranks 48th of forty-nine wards measured, but the source itself grades this figure low confidence, and the middle half of the forty-nine wards measured spans only about five points on this measure, meaning most of the city sits close together here. A near-bottom rank on a shaky, tightly bunched number does not mean the ward is shut out of public investment.

news.headline: Boy, 13, Wounded In Portage Park Drive-By Shooting
news.note: A 13-year-old was shot in the leg on Montrose Avenue in Portage Park, with no arrests reported at the time of the story.

news.headline: Historic Jefferson Park Firehouse Could Be Turned Into Salon Suite For Local Businesses
news.note: A developer proposed converting the ground floor of a 120-year-old firehouse into a shared beauty and wellness space for about 15 local businesses.

news.headline: Jeff Fest Is No More. It's The Chicago Italian Beef Fest Now
news.note: Jefferson Park's 25-year-old music and arts festival was rebranded around Italian beef, with eight vendors set for the late-July event.
